name: Transposition of the Great Arteries
aliases: Complete Transposition of the Great Arteries

criteria.description: Aorta arises from the right ventricle and pulmonary artery arises from the left ventricle (ventriculoarterial discordance)
Parallel course of the great arteries rather than the normal crossing
Presence or absence of associated defects such as ventricular septal defect or patent foramen ovale

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of ventriculoarterial discordance with the aorta arising from the right ventricle and pulmonary artery from the left ventricle on echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically confirmed by echocardiography shortly after birth due to cyanosis and hypoxemia.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
pathognomonic.notes: Usually apparent within hours after birth
searchTerms: central bluish discoloration not improving with oxygen

common.symptomName: Poor feeding and failure to thrive
searchTerms: difficulty feeding and not gaining weight
failure to thrive with feeding problems

common.symptomName: Clubbing of fingers (in older infants if untreated)
Heart murmur due to associated defects
common.notes: May be present if VSD or PDA coexist
searchTerms: abnormal heart sounds from heart problems

rare.symptomName: Seizures secondary to hypoxic brain injury
searchTerms: seizures caused by brain oxygen loss
convulsions after brain injury from low oxygen
epileptic episodes due to hypoxic brain damage

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis
imaging: Chest X-ray showing 'egg on a string' cardiac silhouette
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography for detailed anatomy if needed
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
Occasional association with chromosomal anomalies (e.g., 22q11 deletion)
other: Pulse oximetry screening in newborns for early detection
Electrocardiogram may show right ventricular hypertrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary stenosis with right ventricular outflow obstruction
Overriding aorta and ventricular septal defect
Pulmonary veins drain into systemic venous circulation
Right heart enlargement without ventriculoarterial discordance
Snowman or figure-of-eight sign on chest X-ray

redFlags: Severe cyanosis within hours after birth
Failure to respond to oxygen therapy
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Maron BJ, et al. Braunwald's Heart Disease. 11th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
